D: A car salesman's plan to have his wife kidnapped goes horribly wrong in snowy Minnesota.
P: Serve the buffet when Marge and Norm hit the buffet.
S: Welcome to Brainerd, home of Paul Bunyan

Cheese curds dipped in a light beer batter, fried at 185C for 60 seconds until puffed, ranch dip of sour cream, mayo, dill and chives. Whisk 120g flour with 200ml cold lager. Dip 300g cheese curds and fry at 185C for 60 seconds until puffed. Mix 150g sour cream, 2 tbsp mayo, chopped dill and chives for ranch. Serve hot.
Minnesota hotdish, made in a muffin tin

Beef mince and onion in a creamy mushroom sauce, baked in muffin tins under crunchy tater tots and melted cheddar, with tomato relish. Brown 400g beef mince with 1 diced onion and 150g sliced mushrooms. Stir in 1 tbsp flour, then 200ml milk and 100ml cream and simmer 5 minutes until thick, with salt, pepper and a dash of Worcestershire. Spoon into 12 greased muffin holes. Top each with 3 or 4 frozen tater tots and a pinch of grated cheddar from 100g. Bake at 210C for 25 minutes until the tots are crisp. Serve with tomato relish.
Marge is eating for two at the buffet

Dill pickles, green olives, radishes, celery and carrot sticks on ice with a sour cream and dill dip. Arrange dill pickle spears, green olives, radishes, celery and carrot sticks on a tray of ice. Mix 200g sour cream with chopped dill and salt for a dip. Serve it like a church buffet, you betcha.
M: Marge and Norm at the all-you-can-eat buffet

Topside roasted pink and carved thin, with rich gravy, buttery mashed potato, sweet corn and soft dinner rolls, buffet plates piled high. Rub a 1.5kg beef topside with oil, salt and pepper. Sear in a hot roasting tin, then roast at 200C for 40 to 45 minutes until 52C inside. Rest 20 minutes, then carve thin. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and 100ml milk. Make gravy from the pan juices with 1 tbsp flour and 400ml beef stock. Heat 400g frozen corn with butter. Serve with warm dinner rolls.
Firm white fish (walleye or flathead) in a beer batter, fried at 180C, chips, coleslaw and tartare.
W: any pie will do at the buffet

Granny Smith apples baked with cinnamon and brown sugar in a flaky shortcrust under a lattice, served warm with vanilla ice cream. Peel and slice 1kg Granny Smith apples and toss with 120g brown sugar, 2 tsp cinnamon, 2 tbsp cornflour and the juice of half a lemon. Line a 23cm pie dish with 2 sheets shortcrust pastry and fill. Weave a lattice from 2 more sheets cut into strips, brush with egg and sprinkle with sugar. Bake at 190C for 50 minutes until golden and bubbling. Rest 30 minutes and serve with ice cream.
K: Norm's mallard makes the three-cent stamp

Strong hot coffee whisked with melted dark chocolate and milk, poured from a thermos and topped with maple whipped cream. Brew 500ml strong coffee. Heat 500ml milk in a saucepan until steaming and whisk in 100g chopped dark chocolate and 2 tbsp brown sugar until smooth. Stir in the coffee and pour into a warmed thermos. Whip 150ml thickened cream with 1 tbsp maple syrup to soft peaks. Pour into 4 mugs and spoon the cream on top.
